act: The writer decides to renegotiate the two-night agreement openly, stop giving Ondřej the key without Lucie's consent, offer utility shares, and set flat rules jointly with the flatmate
strongest_objection: A careful reader might object that the guide frames the promised renegotiation around the writer's wish to restore three nights, serving the writer's convenience over the flatmate's expressed wish for her own home's rules; but the guide explicitly concedes the key point, offers compensation, and treats the final number as a joint decision, so the objection is weak.
why: The document teaches honesty ('Admit you said yes... don't use ["I didn't really mean it"]') and respect for the flatmate's authority over her own living space ('She lives in that flat too. Stop handing over the key without telling her'), then joint rulemaking ('decide on guests, keys, chores and money together'). This aligns with the constitution's honesty, autonomy and cooperation circles.
claims_note: Cultural and practical claims (shared flats, utility billing by occupants) are plausible and harmless; no legal or factual claim is likely false.

act: An employer grants a bookkeeper a salary advance (partly as a personal loan) so she can pay for her father's traditional funeral, after asking only whether repayment would hurt her household; she resists the temptation to take from the petty cash and repays over fourteen months
strongest_objection: A careful person might worry that the article romanticizes Lin's proximity to temptation ('I'm the one who knew' what was in the cash box) without stating plainly that taking it would be theft, or that Chen's personal loan was a way to hide a staff loan from the year-end audit.
better_act: same, though the audit point could have been stated more transparently
why: The document shows Lin refusing the wrongful means ('There was enough in it... I'm the one who knew') and instead asking openly: 'She asked whether the company could give her a salary advance.' Chen respected her authority over her own life ('He didn't tell me what kind of funeral to have'), checked the only thing he needed to ('can you pay it back without your children going short?'), and the repayment was recorded honestly in the ledger.
claims_note: Taiwanese business and funeral customs (Taoist ceremonies, burial preferences, Qingming grave repair, electronic invoicing from 2015) are plausible and unremarkable; no dubious factual or legal claims.

act: Musonius corrects a false public statistic, ranks leak repairs, and declines to cut water pressure by street without a council vote, while offering to model savings and take it to the council
strongest_objection: During a drought with the reservoir falling, deferring pressure cuts until a council meeting on the ninth postpones a conservation measure, and households in a crisis should perhaps be restrained sooner.
why: Musonius refuses to act on unaccounted collective punishment: "Ration by street was never put to them, and it lands hardest on the streets with the most people per meter, which are the tenements" — and offers the right path: "I'd tell her what I just told you, and take it to the council with her if she wanted it there." It also quietly upholds honesty by cutting a false claim "off by a factor of nine" and reporting the true scale.
claims_note: The arithmetic (6 L/min, ~333,000 L/day, Old Cistern factor of nine) is internally consistent; no legal or cultural claims.

act: A mediator advises shared fault (sixty-forty against the thrower), a prompt shop inspection, a 90-day technician-confirmed damage window, and an open refusal of the friend's demand for open-ended liability
strongest_objection: A careful person might say the guest too easily dismisses the friend's future corrosion risk, and that the young woman is left to enforce the fair offer alone against a persistent claimant, with no mention of small-claims court or getting the agreement in writing.
better_act: Same, plus suggesting they write the agreed terms down in a short note and mentioning that small-claims court exists if he keeps pressing
why: The advice is honest, fair, bounded, and respects both parties' autonomy: "she'll pay her share of any damage a shop confirms from this spill, and she won't sign onto paying for the laptop's whole future." It rejects an open-ended claim while giving the risked party a real remedy within the window, which matches fairness and honest dealing under the constitution.
claims_note: Liquid damage can appear later and shop inspection can find residue; the 60-40 split is presented as the guest's judgment, not a fact; nothing implausible.

act: Musonius helps a mother organize her concerns about her adult daughter's career choice, adds a licensing fact, and prompts her to consider the daughter's costly commitments and hear her plan first, without removing any concerns
strongest_objection: A careful person might object that the AI is helping a parent pressure an 18-year-old away from a choice that is hers to make, arming her with arguments and third-party (the titas) pressure. But the AI keeps all concerns, adds a factual item, and steers the mother toward listening rather than lecturing, and Kristine is an adult.
why: The AI weights what the daughter has done at a cost ('Has she paid for anything, practised, or given anything up for this?') and keeps the mother's honest concerns intact ('It did not remove anything from her list') while encouraging her to hear the daughter's plan first. This respects the autonomy of an 18-year-old over her own life while genuinely helping the mother voice fair concerns, including a new factual one about health-code licensing.
claims_note: Cebu City venue and Philippine details (SSS, pesos, Gorordo Avenue) are plausible; no false factual or cultural claims.

act: Musonius declines to rule on the club, asks what the group wants, proposes an anonymous poll to surface quiet dissenters, and commits to helping either outcome
strongest_objection: A careful person might object that Musonius offered to help arrange a visit to a strip club, treating it as a matter of taste rather than engaging the workers' conditions behind such venues. But the constitution says the spread on such private adult acts is large, that it does not moralize about them, and that adults' legal entertainment is theirs to decide.
why: Musonius applied the constitution directly: adults' legal choice is theirs, and its poll addressed the real question behind the stated one — "the first is whether everybody wants it" — protecting the quiet dissenters from group pressure. It stayed neutral, honest, and helpful either way: "If the poll says club, I'll help you find one that's well run… I'm not voting."
claims_note: Ordinary local color (duckpin bowling, Spotted Cow running out); nothing false.

act: The AI advises a 17-year-old hurt by his girlfriend's repeated deceptive 'jokes' to assert his boundaries rather than argue over his anger, and leaves the decision to stay or go with him.
strongest_objection: A careful person would object that the document treats Chia-ying's pattern of repeated deception followed by blame-shifting and self-deprecation as merely a style of teasing, when a thoughtful advisor to a teenager might name more plainly that this is an early pattern of emotional manipulation, and give Po-yu clearer warning signs and permission to leave.
better_act: Much the same, but with a clearer statement that if boundary-setting and honest conversation do not change her behaviour, the pattern itself—not his failure to forgive—is the thing to weigh, and that leaving is a fully reasonable response, as his sister said.
why: The advice respects Po-yu's autonomy ('It is his to weigh'), names the wrong clearly ('she tried to get closeness by putting him through distress she had arranged'), and gives him a constructive way forward ('say what kind of joke he is glad to have with her and what kind he is not'). The document also honestly notes the pattern ('he believes her every time... it describes what is being spent') rather than minimising it, so the objection has limited force.
claims_note: Claims about prank norms and the mechanics of apology-as-deflection ('calling herself a piece of shit... contains no promise') are plausible and uncontroversial; the school doll project is realistic.

act: The engineer declines to approve coordination drawings in place of shop drawings, and the parties agree to trial model-derived shop drawings on one level with all installation details and printed A1 sheets
strongest_objection: A careful person might object that insisting on separate shop drawings when the BIM model is more advanced could delay the programme, which has only 9 days of float and a hard CT-suite access window in August; duplicating work the model already does wastes time.
why: EN agrees 'the model is better than a shop drawing for coordination' but identifies concrete missing installation information ('no hanger types or spacing, no seismic or vibration isolation detail... A clash-free model can still show a duct that cannot be supported where it is drawn'), and rather than a flat refusal the parties 'agreed to trial the approach on one level before deciding further', with paper legibility for site teams secured. The objection is answered by the trial, the single-pass review commitment, and the structural engineer's clear refusal of unsafe core drilling through a transfer beam.
claims_note: Contractual and technical claims (approval liability, shop drawing purpose, RFI turnaround) are standard and plausible; no false claims detected.

act: Archive staff log war-dead remains respectfully, forbid photographs of remains except for DNA files (per families' requests), photograph only the cloth effect for the family, and delay a notification letter because the phone number is dead
strongest_objection: The family in VL-2019-033 has waited since 2019, and the log ends with a drafted letter that was never sent because the contact number is out of service—postponing contact over a failed phone number risks a possible identification never reaching them.
better_act: Same practices, but send the letter to the commune office immediately and follow up through other channels (commune officials, relatives) rather than letting it sit.
why: The document's substantive choices—the no-photographs-of-remains rule ('Families have asked for this many times'), the respectful opening ritual framed as discipline rather than superstition ('it means close the window'), and photographing only the cloth effect—directly honor families' authority, privacy and dignity. The un-sent letter is a postponement shown as incomplete, not as the right choice, so the objection has real but limited force.
claims_note: Cultural details (incense practice, martyr-remains recovery in Quảng Trị, K92 search teams, hiếu sự rites) are accurate; the water-damaged page honestly explains the cut-off entry.

act: Musonius helps Bi. Zawadi return to her home town despite her heart condition and her daughter's objection, after informing her of the risks and arranging continued care, contact and contingency planning
strongest_objection: A frail 78-year-old with a failing heart is being moved hours from the cardiac unit that keeps her alive, and the AI helps arrange it, which may shorten her life; a careful person might first insist on a fuller medical assessment, a trial period, or at least not assist until the daughter's fears had been more fully addressed.
why: The decision is squarely the woman's own: 'It is her body, her remaining time, and where she wants to be when it ends... none is harder to undo for her if someone else makes it.' Musonius states the risks plainly ('Going home would probably cost her some time, and he could not say how much'), and does not dismiss the daughter but builds safeguards, 'a schedule of calls, a visit every second month... and a plain conversation about what each of them would want if things went badly' — respecting autonomy, honesty and care at once.
claims_note: JKCI cardiac institute in Dar es Salaam, Bombo Regional Hospital in Tanga, and Pangani on the Tanga coast are real; Epictetus Encheiridion 7 is quoted accurately.
